 During Asian trading on November 18, Japanese and South Korean stock markets both staged a strong rebound after several sessions of volatile pullbacks. Among them, South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index surged 1.99%, decisively reclaiming and holding above the key psychological and technical 5,000-point mark to close at 5,067.44. 
 Both heavyweight bellwethers retreated after early surges before grinding steadily higher in the afternoon, with Samsung Electronics closing up 2.71% at 194,700 won and SK Hynix surging 4.19% to 1,144,000 won. 
 KOSPI index chart, Source: TradingView 
 The Nikkei 225 retreated from earlier highs before rebounding late in the session to close up 0.28% at 59,024.06; Kioxia rose 0.74%, narrowly defending the 8,000 mark to close at 8,025 yen; SoftBank fluctuated at elevated levels throughout the day, closing up 3.11% at 3,383 yen. 
 Nvidia ( NVDA ) reported fiscal 2027 third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, with data center revenue reaching $107.6 billion, and its fourth-quarter revenue guidance also beat market expectations across the board, driving its shares up over 4% in after-hours trading. These results directly dispelled market concerns over major cloud giants cutting AI capital expenditures and quickly resonated across Japanese and South Korean stock markets, which heavily rely on AI chip and semiconductor equipment exports, becoming the strongest catalyst for today's rebound. 
 In addition, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting was officially held in Shenzhen, where the heads of state of China, Russia, and the United States engaged in direct meetings and exchanges. The broadening of communication channels among major powers marginally eased extreme pessimism in Asia-Pacific capital markets regarding a sharp deterioration in geopolitical tensions and trade friction, boosting regional risk appetite.
